units.text: The proposed approach for using GNNs for bacterial communities is vaguely described and not well justified.
The key methods section (2.2) provides a generic description of existing GNN approaches, and is missing key microbiome specific information (in particular, what is the topology of the graph).
That information is provided in Supplementary information: the graph is fully connected.
This makes statements in the manuscript such as “By using k graph convolutional layers after one another we can achieve k-hop information propagation” rather misleading.
Overall, the proposed method - applying GNN model in a straightforward way to a very small, fully-connected graph - is poorly justified and weak on novelty.
What is the rationale for using a GNN on a very simple graph?
What is the benefit of focusing on predicting steady state, instead of focusing on dynamical changes to the relative abundances (e.g., dysbiosis).
